title: Fractal correlation properties of heart rate variability and respiratory frequency as measures of endurance exercise durability
authors: Rogers B, Fleitas-Paniagua PR, Trpcic M, Zagatto AM, Murias JM
population: Ten participants performing cycling time-to-task-failure at 95% of respiratory compensation point on two occasions (control and monetary reward)
findings: After initial equilibration, metabolic responses (VO2, lactate, glucose) remained largely stable over quarters 2 to 4 of the trial.
HR, DFA-a1 and respiratory frequency each drifted over Q2-Q4 (significant ANOVA).
Repeatability of quarterly HR, DFA-a1 and respiratory frequency between control and reward sessions was high: ICC 0.73 to 0.94, Pearson r 0.83 to 0.98, no difference in means.
The authors conclude these are useful, repeatable markers of durability loss that could be monitored with low-cost consumer equipment.
limitations: Ten participants, cycling, laboratory time-to-failure at a single intensity; running, heat, hydration and comparison against performance outcomes were not tested; the ICC range is pooled over three metrics, not HR alone.
implications: Within-session HR drift at steady intensity was repeatable in this cycling study (ICC 0.73-0.94 pooled across HR, DFA-a1 and respiratory frequency), so computing and storing it per run is reasonable, but its link to performance must be checked in the athlete's own data.
Treat DFA-a1 and respiratory-frequency features as optional, device-dependent extras, not core plan inputs.

verification.notes: Crossref (online 2025-02-04, print 2025 Jun) and PubMed match. Corrected the researcher's attribution of the ICC range to HR alone; the abstract pools HR, DFA-a1 and fB. Dropped the unsupported 'healthy' descriptor.
